learningObjective: Given an elementwise kernel's per-element FLOP and byte cost, compute the arithmetic intensity and classify the kernel against a specific GPU's FP32 ridge point.
stem: On A100 SXM (peak FP32 ≈ 19.5 TFLOP/s, HBM ≈ 2.0 TB/s), a kernel reads an FP32 tensor A of shape [32M] and writes B[i] = softplus(A[i]) (≈ 10 FLOPs per element). Which Roofline analysis is correct?

options.text: Compute-bound; the 10 FLOPs per element push arithmetic intensity above the FP32 ridge point, so the achievable ceiling is close to the A100 FP32 peak of 19.5 TFLOP/s.
Memory-bound; AI = 10/8 = 1.25 FLOP/byte < A100 FP32 ridge (~ 9.75); ceiling ≈ 2.5 TFLOP/s.
Memory-bound; arithmetic intensity ≈ 2.5 FLOP/byte, obtained by counting only the input reads and ignoring the output writes since writes are asynchronous on the memory bus.
Compute-bound; achievable throughput ≈ 19.5 TFLOP/s because element-wise kernels always saturate the SM math pipelines once occupancy exceeds 50%.

explanation: Per element: 10 FLOPs; 4 bytes read + 4 bytes written = 8 bytes. Arithmetic intensity = 10/8 = 1.25 FLOP/byte. A100 FP32 ridge point = 19.5 TFLOP/s / 2.0 TB/s = 9.75 FLOP/byte. AI (1.25) < ridge (9.75) → memory-bound. Ceiling = AI × BW = 1.25 × 2.0 = 2.5 TFLOP/s.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: 10 FLOPs per element only yields AI ≈ 1.25 FLOP/byte, still far below the ridge point; the kernel remains memory-bound.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: AI = FLOPs / (read+write bytes) = 10/8 = 1.25 FLOP/byte; ceiling = AI × HBM BW.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: correct classification (memory-bound) but the AI is miscomputed by omitting output-write bytes; proper streaming AI counts read + write traffic.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: element-wise kernels do not automatically saturate math pipelines; without high AI they saturate HBM instead.

assumptions: No cache reuse: each byte of A is read from HBM exactly once, each byte of B is written to HBM exactly once.
Softplus operates on a single tensor and does not fuse with adjacent ops in this measurement.
nonImplications: Does not imply that fusing softplus with a neighboring elementwise op has no benefit; fusion can reduce bytes moved and lift throughput.
Does not imply that FP16 softplus would be compute-bound; it would still be memory-bound, just with different AI.

distractorRationales.A: Overestimates the effect of adding math to an elementwise kernel.
distractorRationales.C: Common AI arithmetic error: counting only reads.

performanceClaim.scope: A100 SXM, FP32 elementwise softplus over 32 M elements, streaming
